question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I read the guide, then package query help to learn the command syntax and candidate limit. I used -Q and -Q Packages to find the depends and dependency-target filters and learn whether depends covered direct or indirect dependencies. I first tried a depth-enabled 40-candidate query to capture either kind, but the command rejected that combination because depth limits inspection to five candidates. I then ran a 40-candidate direct-dependency query for Microsoft.Extensions.* with Polly and net10.0, and viewed its JSON for package version, manifest dependency group, and selected framework, plus stderr for completion status. That gave one supported direct match and an explicit warning that the family was not exhausted. A further package read would only have repeated manifest facts already in the JSON; a narrower depth search might have found indirect examples but would not establish completeness for the 40-candidate family search. Since the task allowed up to three and required stating uncertainty, I stopped there.
